findings.text: a git alias name is outside MUTATING_VERBS, so `git -C <other> -c alias.zap='reset --hard HEAD~1' zap` is allowed and the reset lands in the other checkout (probe E2E, guard-bypass-probe.log).

an inline environment assignment is not parsed, so `GIT_DIR=<other>/.git GIT_WORK_TREE=<other> git reset --hard` falls back to the segment cwd inside the worktree and is allowed (probe E2E moved the other checkout's HEAD).

cd tracking recognises only a cd that begins its segment after "(" tokens, so `$(cd <other> && git reset --hard)`, backticks, `bash -c '...'`, `{ cd <other>; ...; }` and `X=1 cd <other>` leave the cwd stale and are allowed.

the landed installer entry is reachable only from tests; reckon/cli.py:162 (_configure_crew_guards) wires the two sibling guards through its own composer, so approving the install later needs new wiring rather than the include_git_guard flag alone.
